subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should the repository intentionally ship the `question.*` and session-catalog breaking changes in the next beta under the claimed unshipped/beta-only compatibility window, before `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` is published publicly?
rationale: The branch changes externally consumable protocol names, answer shapes, and exports. The PR body asserts the affected surfaces are unshipped or beta-only, but accepting that release contract is a maintainer decision rather than a mechanical code-review conclusion.

options.title: Approve the pre-publication break window
options.body: Accept the audited beta-only protocol changes and require current-head generated-client plus real gateway/client proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve beta compatibility temporarily
options.body: Keep aliases or a documented migration window until the next beta release train, then remove the old shapes in a follow-up.

options.title: Pause the publication cleanup
options.body: Defer the API reshaping until maintainers can establish the intended package and beta compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the pre-publication break window
recommendation.body: Accept the audited beta-only protocol changes and require current-head generated-client plus real gateway/client proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied commit history and PR body show direct ownership of the protocol-release-train proposal and its cross-client migration.
